title: Are these four statements about mean and median always true?
description: Four statements about removing or including values are tested on small lists. Each is judged to be always true, sometimes true or never true, with a reason from where the middle value or the balance point moves.
teaching_notes: One idea: one small list can show a statement is not always true, and a reason about the middle or the balance point shows it is always or never true. Watch for students who call a statement always true after checking only one example.

source: Figure it Out (mean and median, question 6)
video_script.why: A child who has seen the median and the mean move when a value is included now judges general statements about them.
video_script.substitution: the book's four statements, tested on the small list 1, 2, 3 and a second list
video_script.anchor: a small row of dots 1, 2, 3 with the median marked and the mean as a balance point
video_script.payoff_line: The answers are never, always, sometimes and never

final_answer.spoken: the answers are never, always, sometimes and never

never_show: a statement marked always true from one example alone
maths_rules: (i) 1, 2, 3 has median 2; removing 1 leaves 2, 3 with median 2.5; removing a value below the median moves the median up or leaves it, so never true
(ii) 4, 6 has mean 5; including 2 gives total 12 over 3 values, mean 4; a value below the mean always lowers the mean, so always true
(iii) 1, 2, 3 plus 0, 0, 10, 10 sorted is 0, 0, 1, 2, 3, 10, 10 with median 2 (unchanged); 1, 2, 3 plus 10, 10, 10, 10 sorted is 1, 2, 3, 10, 10, 10, 10 with median 10 (changed); so sometimes true
(iv) 1, 2, 3 plus four 0s sorted is 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 2, 3 with median 0 (lower, not higher); values below the median never raise it, so never true
check: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 has median 3; plus four 0s sorted is 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and the 5th value is 1, so the median fell from 3 to 1
video_script.design: One row of dots all video. For each statement a test list is built from the same dots, one value is removed or included, and the median marker or the balance point is watched.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; four statement cards about median and mean, each with an empty box for always, sometimes or never

marks.book: the title card From your book appears
marks.ask: the three words always, sometimes, never appear beside the cards

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the median and the mean.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Four statements are given. The first says removing a value less than the median will decrease the median.
<bookmark mark='second'/>The second says including a value less than the mean will decrease the mean.
<bookmark mark='third'/>The third says including any four values will not affect the median.
<bookmark mark='fourth'/>The fourth says including four values less than the median will increase the median.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Is each one always true, sometimes true, or never true?

beats.on_screen: the four statement cards and the question stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: always true: holds for every list; sometimes true: holds for some lists; never true: fails for every list; test on small lists

marks.always: a tick appears for every list under always true
marks.some: a tick and a cross appear under sometimes true
marks.never: a cross appears for every list under never true
marks.small: a small list of dots 1, 2, 3 appears

narration: <bookmark mark='always'/>Always true means the statement holds for every list.
<bookmark mark='some'/>Sometimes true means it holds for some lists and fails for others.
<bookmark mark='never'/>Never true means it fails for every list.
<bookmark mark='small'/>We test each statement on small lists and look for a reason.

beats.on_screen: Given: four statements about the median and the mean
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, four statements about the median and the mean.

beats.on_screen: To find: always, sometimes or never true, with a reason for each

marks.find: the words always, sometimes, never are written with a reason line

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to judge each statement and give a reason.

beats.on_screen: first: 1, 2, 3 has median 2; remove 1: 2, 3 has median 2.5, which is up, not down

marks.list: the list 1, 2, 3 appears with the median 2 marked
marks.remove: the dot at 1 is removed and the marker moves to 2.5
marks.up: an up arrow appears beside the marker
marks.why: the words never true are written

narration: <bookmark mark='list'/>Step one, test the first statement with one, two and three. The median is two.
<bookmark mark='remove'/>Remove one, which is less than the median. Two and three are left, and the median is two point five.
<bookmark mark='up'/>The median went up, not down.
<bookmark mark='why'/>Taking out a low value pushes the middle up or leaves it. The first statement is never true.

beats.on_screen: second: 4, 6 has mean 5; include 2: (4 + 6 + 2) ÷ 3 = 4, which is down

marks.list: the list 4, 6 appears with the mean 5 marked
marks.join: a dot at 2 joins and the balance marker moves to 4
marks.why: the words always true are written

narration: <bookmark mark='list'/>Step two, test the second statement. Four and six have a mean of five.
<bookmark mark='join'/>Include two, which is less than the mean. Four, six and two have a mean of four.
<bookmark mark='why'/>The mean went down. A value below the mean always pulls the mean down, so the second statement is always true.

beats.on_screen: third: 1, 2, 3 plus 0, 0, 10, 10 has median 2, unchanged; 1, 2, 3 plus 10, 10, 10, 10 has median 10, changed

marks.low: the list 1, 2, 3 appears with the median 2 marked
marks.zeros: 0, 0, 10, 10 join the list and the median stays at 2
marks.high: 10, 10, 10, 10 join the list 1, 2, 3 and the median jumps to 10
marks.some: the words sometimes true are written

narration: <bookmark mark='low'/>Step three, test the third statement two ways. Take one, two and three, with median two.
<bookmark mark='zeros'/>Include zero, zero, ten and ten, and the median is still two.
<bookmark mark='high'/>Include ten, ten, ten and ten instead, and the median becomes ten.
<bookmark mark='some'/>It holds for some choices and fails for others, so the third statement is sometimes true.

beats.on_screen: fourth: 1, 2, 3 plus 0, 0, 0, 0 sorted is 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 2, 3 with median 0, which is down

marks.zeros: four dots at 0 join the list 1, 2, 3
marks.why: the words never true are written

narration: <bookmark mark='zeros'/>Step four, test the fourth statement. Take one, two and three, and include four zeros.
<bookmark mark='mid'/>The sorted list has seven values, and the middle one is zero. The median went down from two to zero.
<bookmark mark='why'/>Values below the median never push it up, so the fourth statement is never true.

beats.on_screen: check: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 has median 3; plus 0, 0, 0, 0 the 5th of 9 values is 1, so the median fell

marks.second: the list 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 appears with the median 3 marked
marks.fall: four zeros join and the marker falls to 1

narration: <bookmark mark='second'/>Check the fourth statement with a second list. One, two, three, four, five has a median of three.
<bookmark mark='fall'/>Include four zeros, and the fifth of nine values is one. The median fell again.

marks.ans: the four judgements are boxed in order

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The answers are never, always, sometimes and never.
